first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly, top to bottom. The opening is plain and tells me what is on the page, which I like. It is mostly pretty weddings until about halfway, and then it finally gets to the questions I actually care about. I am glad it is Australia, so at least I am not worrying about contracts in euros, but nobody has said a word yet about my mother getting from the car to her seat.

journey.quote: After the cards come the questions these weddings raise for any Australian venue, then the legal first step for marrying here.
journey.reaction: Good. Tells me there is something practical coming and I will not just be looking at flowers.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor can plan a wedding anywhere in Australia or abroad and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: Quotes in Australian dollars is what I want to hear. But who is this Advisor? A name, a phone number? It does not say.

journey.quote: On a reef island, the water, the planting and the light arrive before a single flower is brought in.
journey.reaction: I read that twice and I am still not sure what it means. The light arrives? Bit too clever for me.

journey.quote: Each point below ends in questions to put to a venue before you sign, and the answers belong in writing.
journey.reaction: Yes. Exactly right. Get it in writing. This is the first line that sounds like someone sensible wrote it. I would want deposits and refunds on that list too though.

journey.section: Guests travelling from interstate and overseas
journey.quote: Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car?
journey.reaction: Closest the page gets to thinking about older guests. A drop-off point is fine, but can Mum with her walking frame get from there to the clifftop or the croquet lawn? Steps, gravel, a toilet she can reach? Nothing.

journey.section: A ceremony outdoors and a covered plan
journey.quote: Who decides to move under cover, and how many hours before the ceremony?
journey.reaction: Good question, someone accountable. I would also want to know who I actually ring on the day if things go wrong.

journey.section: Styling that lets the setting lead
journey.quote: What can we bring in ourselves, and what has to come from the venue's own suppliers?
journey.reaction: Sensible. That is where the money disappears, the extras you did not know you had to buy from the venue.

journey.quote: What follows is general information, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Clear and honest. The month-to-18-months rule is set out plainly. I can forward this bit to my husband and he will understand it.

journey.quote: Sunscreen goes on at least 20 minutes before heading outside, and again every two hours or after a swim or heavy sweating.
journey.reaction: Bit much to be told how to put on sunscreen, I am from Melbourne. But the point about water and shade for the guests is fair, especially for the older ones sitting out at an afternoon ceremony.

journey.section: Plan your Australian wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: This is the best line on the page for me. One person, fee in writing before anything starts. If it had a name and said I could speak to them on the phone first, I would be much more comfortable.

journey.section: Plan your Australian wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Share with Wedded Concierge the setting you picture, the month you are weighing, your guest numbers and how far everyone will travel.
journey.reaction: Share how? A form? A call? I would not hand over anything until I have spoken to a person. It does not tell me what happens next.

unanswered_questions: Will I get a phone call with a real person before anything is booked, and what is the Advisor's name?
When a Wedded Advisor handles payments, how are deposits held, and are they protected if a venue or supplier lets us down?
What happens to the money if the date has to move or be cancelled?
Who do we ring on the wedding day itself if something goes wrong?
Can elderly guests with walking frames get to the ceremony and reception at these kinds of settings, and will anyone check that for us?
Should we be taking out insurance, and does the Advisor help with that?
How is the Wedded Advisor's fee worked out, roughly?

turn_offs_found.quote: Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car?
turn_offs_found.why: The only nod to older guests, and it stops at the car door. No mention of step-free access, mobility or seating for elderly relatives anywhere on the page.

turn_offs_found.quote: Each point below ends in questions to put to a venue before you sign, and the answers belong in writing.
turn_offs_found.why: Good start, but none of the questions that follow mention deposits, refunds or cancellation, which is what I would want in writing first.

would_share_with: My husband, with the legal steps and the venue questions marked
My daughter, asking her whether she has checked access for her grandmother

cta_reaction.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact from start to finish, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: One accountable person and a written fee is what I want. But I would only go further if I knew I could speak to someone on the phone first and understood how deposits are handled. More likely I would tell my daughter to ring them and report back.

top_3_changes: OLD: "- Is there a drop-off point for guests who arrive by coach or car?" NEW: "- Is there a drop-off point close to the ceremony for guests who arrive by coach or car, and is there step-free access from there to the ceremony, the reception and the bathrooms for older guests or anyone using a walking frame or wheelchair?"

OLD: "Each point below ends in questions to put to a venue before you sign, and the answers belong in writing." NEW: "Each point below ends in questions to put to a venue before you sign, and the answers belong in writing, along with what the deposit covers, when each payment falls due and what happens to your money if the date has to move."

OLD: "- Is that space on the same property, and can we see it set up during our visit?" NEW: "- Is that space on the same property, and can we see it set up during our visit?\n- Who is our contact at the venue on the day, and how do we reach them if something goes wrong?"

open_questions.question: Can the page state how a first conversation with Wedded Concierge happens (for example whether a phone call is offered before booking) and how deposits are handled? Only if the brand source confirms it; I have not assumed either.
